text:
We turned on a CDN and users in Tokyo still waited on our Virginia origin.

Then we cached the wrong API response. A user in Berlin briefly saw someone else's dashboard header.

A CDN is not a performance toggle. It's a shared cache at the edge — and shared caches need explicit rules.

What I got wrong:

• Treating dynamic `/api/me` like static JS
• Forgetting `Cache-Control` on the origin (the CDN does what headers say)
• Purging everything on every deploy instead of fingerprinting assets

Static with hashed filenames → long TTL at the edge. Session-specific JSON → private, no-store. Different hostnames for static vs API helps keep that straight.

Edge hit = origin never touched. Miss = you pay the round trip. First request to each PoP can feel slower until it warms.

Wrote the full post on TTL, purge, origin shield, and the headers that actually matter.

https://blog.sandeepallala.com/blog/system-design-cdn-and-edge-caching
